evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 形義通解; 字音; cited glosses
evidence.text: The database analyzes 忙 as 从心、亡声, with original sense “inner urgency” (內心急迫). It cites 集韻《唐韻》, “忙，心迫也,” and records later uses for being occupied with many tasks (北魏《齊民要術》) and doing something quickly (《兒女英雄傳》). It gives 廣韻 fanqie 莫郎 and Middle Chinese category 明母、平聲、宕攝唐韻、開口一等. This supports the compound analysis and attested sense distinctions, but does not establish a precise date for the cited 集韻 gloss or the earliest occurrence of 忙.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 忙

evidence.source: 中華民國教育部《異體字字典》 (Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants)
evidence.text: The entry says 忙 is not recorded in 說文, identifies its structure as 心-radical with three additional strokes, and notes that the right side of 忄 is written as 亡. Its listed meanings include “many affairs, no free time,” “urgent/panicked,” and “doing something urgently”; it cites 集韻 for 心迫 and later literary examples. Its historical-form table lists references such as 玉篇, 廣韻 and 集韻, but the relevant early glyph images are not supplied as readable text here. No evidence in this entry establishes an older graphic ancestor, a corruption, or a chronology of the shape.

gaps: No inspected primary paleographic image or securely dated early inscriptional attestation for 忙 was found. The available sources do not establish its earliest graphic form, a corruption hypothesis, or the date when the 心迫 sense first appeared.

The semantic path from inner urgency to being occupied with many tasks is plausible from the dictionary’s separately cited senses, but the cited sources do not explicitly document when or how that extension developed. The CUHK database quotes an undated-in-this-view 集韻 gloss; the MOE entry provides later literary examples without enough bibliographic dating here to establish a full chronology.

The local Baxter–Sagart rows support a same-system comparison (*mˤaŋ for 忙 and *maŋ for 亡), but official Unicode Unihan pages and exact current kMandarin entries could not be inspected. No verified online primary source was found here that independently supplies historical reconstructions for both characters.

The inspected evidence supports 亡 as a sound component in 忙, not a whole-graph phonetic loan. No borrowing of the whole 忙 graph is proposed. No independent claim about the original referent or name behind 亡 is necessary for the compound analysis.

No evidence here classifies 忄 as an independently sourced historical ancestor or nonchronological variant of 心; the sources describe it as the semantic component/heart radical. No distinct origin_form relationship is therefore asserted.

Search volume remained within the initial bounded pass; no additional query was made because the accessible dictionary evidence supports the main analysis and remaining paleographic and Unihan questions are recorded as gaps.

No primary paleographic glyph candidate with a verified direct image and character-specific provenance was established. The Commons result inspected is a modern stroke-order drawing, not an ancient artifact image.
A character-specific Xiaoxuetang 忙 form record could not be inspected; the database interface search result did not establish that it contains a usable record for 忙. No Xiaoxuetang image is selected.

The inspected material does not establish 忙's earliest attested occurrence or the date when its “inner urgency” sense first appears. The cited 集韻 gloss is attributed by the MOE entry, but this pass did not inspect a dated manuscript or edition to resolve chronology.
The listed meanings suggest urgency and being occupied as distinct uses, but the inspected source does not document when or through what semantic steps one developed from the other.

This pass did not verify the compound analysis against an accessible full etymological entry, nor inspect exact local Baxter–Sagart and Unihan kMandarin rows. No reconstruction comparison is newly asserted here.
The attempted Unihan record URLs for both 忙 and 亡 failed to open in the web tool. Their current readings and the official click-through evidence remain unverified.
